sections.heading: 1. Office snapshot received
sections.guidance: Sentinel has a current standards pack + type catalogue from the office template (sent from Revit via Build Office System → Send office snapshot).

sections.heading: 2. Naming rules exist for families, types, views and sheets
sections.guidance: The office ruleset carries token rules for every target and an office code.

sections.heading: 3. Template types follow the type convention
sections.guidance: Wall/floor/ceiling/roof/door/window types in the template match the type-naming rules.

sections.heading: 4. Worksets follow the office whitelist
sections.guidance: Every whitelisted workset exists in the template; no extras.

sections.heading: 5. Required shared parameters exist
sections.guidance: Parameters the rules and family gate rely on are bound in the template.

sections.heading: 6. Live model health
sections.guidance: The latest scan of a live project model shows no blocking violations and few warnings.

sections.heading: 7. Container naming standard installed
sections.guidance: An ISO 19650 container naming ruleset is installed for the office project.

sections.heading: 8. Family library has a custodian and a location
sections.question: Is there one named person responsible for the family library, and one agreed location where approved families live?

sections.heading: 9. Revit template is versioned and owned
sections.question: Does the office template have a version number, a change log and an owner who approves changes?

sections.heading: 10. Office modelling guideline exists
sections.question: Is there a written modelling guideline (what to model, how, at which stage) that modellers actually use?
sections.answer_hint: partial = exists but unused or outdated

sections.heading: 11. Project roles present: owner and lead
sections.guidance: The office project has at least one owner and one lead in Sentinel.

sections.heading: 12. Task teams declared per discipline, each with a lead
sections.guidance: Task teams are registered with an accountable lead.

sections.heading: 13. A BIM manager is named and accountable
sections.question: Is there a named BIM manager with the mandate to stop a delivery that fails the standard?

sections.heading: 14. Coordinators named per discipline
sections.question: Does each discipline have a named BIM coordinator?

sections.heading: 15. Modellers trained on the template
sections.question: Have the modellers been trained on the office template and naming, with a record of who attended?

sections.heading: 16. Onboarding for new staff exists
sections.question: Is there an onboarding path for new BIM staff (template, standards, CDE access) that runs without the BIM manager present?

sections.heading: 17. Time is budgeted for information management
sections.question: Do project budgets carry hours for information management (BEP, MIDP, checks, coordination) separately from modelling?

sections.heading: 18. Responsibility matrix agreed with clients
sections.question: Is a responsibility matrix (who produces, who checks, who accepts) agreed with the client on current projects?

sections.heading: 19. A BEP exists and is executable
sections.guidance: A BEP document exists in Sentinel and at least half of its clauses control production (executability score).

sections.heading: 20. CDE states in use
sections.guidance: Containers move through WIP → Shared → Published.

sections.heading: 21. Container names conform
sections.guidance: Published containers follow the naming ruleset.

sections.heading: 22. Task-team responsibility on deliverables
sections.guidance: Every planned deliverable names a declared task team with a lead.

sections.heading: 23. Reviews happen before Shared
sections.question: Is every container checked by someone before it is shared with other teams?

sections.heading: 24. Authorisation before Published is separate from submission
sections.question: Is the person who authorises a publish different from the person who submitted it?

sections.heading: 25. EIR received and read for current projects
sections.question: For current projects, has the client's EIR been received and turned into concrete requirements the team knows?

sections.heading: 26. MIDP maintained against the programme
sections.question: Is there a delivery plan with dates that tracks the construction programme and is updated when it moves?

sections.heading: 27. Issues tracked in one place
sections.question: Are coordination issues tracked in one system with status and owner, not in emails?

sections.heading: 28. Models exchanged as IFC with a delivery gate
sections.question: Are models exchanged as IFC, and checked against requirements before they leave the office?

sections.heading: 29. Handover deliverables defined
sections.question: Is it defined what the client receives at handover (asset information, formats, structure)?

sections.heading: 30. Lessons learned recorded per project
sections.question: Are lessons learned recorded at project close and fed back into the template and standards?
